working_definition: Neuroblasts (dpn+, ase+) of the wandering third instar larval optic lobe, derived from the neuroepithelium, that divide asymmetrically to produce ganglion mother cells and medulla/lobula plate neurons.

best_match.fbbt_definition: Neuroblast that generates neurons of the optic lobe. It arises from the optic lobe neuroepithelium, with some delaminating during the embryonic stage and others delaminating during the larval stage (Hakes et al., 2018).

justification: The authors name unsubdivided neuroblasts of the optic lobe; optic neuroblast is exact for label plus tissue. Not narrowed to larval optic neuroblast (curator 2026-10-16): optic neuroblasts delaminate during the embryonic or the larval stage, and the paper does not say which these are (neuroblasts in a wandering L3 optic lobe may be either). Not narrowed to medulla forming neuroblast because the authors' label does not say so (the set also includes a lobula plate-class cluster).

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Neuroblast that delaminates from the optic lobe neuroepithelium during the larval stage (Egger et al., 2007). It generates secondary (adult-specific) optic lobe neurons via asymmetric division (Egger et al., 2007).
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Defined by delamination during the larval stage; the paper does not say when these neuroblasts delaminated (curator 2026-10-16).

other_candidates.fbbt_definition:
Can be distinguished from other optic lobe neuroblasts based on expression of dpn and ase (Konstantinides et al., 2022).
A neuroblast that is the precursor of the medulla. The neuroblasts that give rise to the outer medulla neurons are located in the medial edge of the larval outer optic anlage, whereas the neuroblasts that give rise to the inner medulla neurons are located in the larval inner optic anlage.
other_candidates.reason_rejected: More specific than the authors' label 'neuroblasts'.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Precursor of the central nervous system that derives from the neurogenic region of the ectoderm or the mesectoderm (Doe, 1992; Schmid et al., 1999; Crews, 2019). It produces neurons and/or glia (Doe, 1992; Beckervordersandforth et al., 2008). Neuroblasts may also divide during adult life to regenerate the adult brain (Fernandez-Hernandez et al., 2013).
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Too generic; the optic lobe term is exact.
